rv.q: The result is the best solution - that is, one need not have seen a single frame of the film (called "The Celebration" in this country) to appreciate the engrossing, aching, classic Greek inevitability of the family dynamics.
Otherwise, this empty house is still waiting to be haunted.

But it needs at its center a family that has grown almost violently close in struggling to prevent shattering under the actions of its patriarch; this Festen has a group of people, and actors, who aren't believably bound together by anything.

cn.t: Rufus Norris's staging earns praise for its intensity and austere design, but the domestic drama suffers from indifferent acting that undermines the dark family reunion at its core. Mixed reviews overall.

vs.sum: The Music Box Theatre offers excellent sightlines from most seats, making it ideal for intimate dramas, though sound quality can vary. The theater's charming Georgian-inspired design adds to its ambiance, while comfort and facilities are average for a Broadway venue.

acc.note: 5 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No steps from sidewalk. Infrared devices available.
